## Threshold sensitivity

*Addresses Reviewer 1, comment 2: discrete cut-offs make a site scoring 0.4999 "out"
and one scoring 0.5001 "in".* We sweep both thresholds and report how the headline
conclusions move.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
cantley <- fread(
  here("results", "unfiltered_cantley_dataset.csv"),
  select = c("Substrate_Uniprot_ID", "Substrate", "Substrate_entrez",
             "Kinase", "Kinase_entrez", "Percentile", "promiscuity_index",
             "Site", "residue", "position"),
  colClasses = list(character = c("Substrate_entrez", "Kinase_entrez"))
)
cantley <- cantley[!is.na(Kinase) & !is.na(Percentile)]

ochoa <- fread(here("results", "ochoa_functional_scores.csv"))
setnames(ochoa, c("Substrate_Uniprot_ID", "position", "functional_score"))

hpa <- read_tsv(here("data", "CantleyData", "subcellular_location.tsv"),
                show_col_types = FALSE)
```
:::

```{.r .cell-code}
hpa_long <- hpa %>%
  select(-Gene) %>%
  rename(Gene = `Gene name`) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(contains("Approved"), contains("Supported"), contains("Enhanced")),
               names_to = "tier", values_to = "locs") %>%
  filter(!is.na(locs)) %>%
  separate_rows(locs, sep = ";") %>%
  mutate(locs = str_trim(locs)) %>%
  filter(locs != "") %>%
  distinct(Gene, locs)

# Key on Entrez IDs, exactly as the pipeline does: gene symbols are not stable
# across HPA, the atlases and the curated databases. HPA genes with no Entrez ID
# are dropped, because an NA key would match any other NA key.
hpa_entrez <- suppressMessages(
  clusterProfiler::bitr(unique(hpa_long$Gene), fromType = "SYMBOL", toType = "ENTREZID",
                        OrgDb = org.Hs.eg.db::org.Hs.eg.db))
hpa_long <- hpa_long %>%
  inner_join(hpa_entrez, by = c("Gene" = "SYMBOL")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(ENTREZID)) %>%
  distinct(Gene_entrez = ENTREZID, locs)

coloc_ok_pairs <- {
  kin <- hpa_long %>% rename(Kinase_entrez = Gene_entrez)
  sub <- hpa_long %>% rename(Substrate_entrez = Gene_entrez)
  inner_join(kin, sub, by = "locs", relationship = "many-to-many") %>%
    distinct(Kinase_entrez, Substrate_entrez)
}
```
:::

```{.r .cell-code}
promiscuity_cutoff <- quantile(cantley$promiscuity_index, 0.5, na.rm = TRUE)

# Curated-site status, so the sweep applies the same rule as the pipeline:
# co-localized AND (curated site OR functional score above cut-off).
kinet <- read_csv(here("data", "kinet_data", "ksi_source_full_dataset.csv"),
                  show_col_types = FALSE)
curated_site_keys <- kinet %>%
  transmute(Substrate_Uniprot_ID = str_remove(Substrate, "-\\d+$"),
            Site = str_trim(Site)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Substrate_Uniprot_ID), !is.na(Site)) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  mutate(key = paste(Substrate_Uniprot_ID, Site, sep = ":")) %>%
  pull(key)

annot <- cantley[promiscuity_index < promiscuity_cutoff &
                   !is.na(Kinase_entrez) & !is.na(Substrate_entrez)]
annot <- merge(annot, ochoa, by = c("Substrate_Uniprot_ID", "position"), all.x = TRUE)
annot <- merge(annot, as.data.table(coloc_ok_pairs)[, coloc := TRUE],
               by = c("Kinase_entrez", "Substrate_entrez"), all.x = TRUE)
annot[is.na(coloc), coloc := FALSE]
annot[, curated_site := paste(Substrate_Uniprot_ID, Site, sep = ":") %in% curated_site_keys]

# Dark status by Entrez ID (DarkKinaseTools still uses superseded symbols for a few genes)
dark_kin <- all_kinases %>% filter(class_2019 == "Dark") %>% pull(entrez_id) %>% as.character()

sweep_grid <- expand_grid(
  motif_cut = c(80, 85, 90, 95, 99),
  func_cut  = c(0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7)
)

sweep <- sweep_grid %>%
  pmap_dfr(function(motif_cut, func_cut) {
    keep <- annot[Percentile >= motif_cut & coloc == TRUE &
                    (curated_site == TRUE |
                       (!is.na(functional_score) & functional_score >= func_cut))]
    pairs <- unique(keep[, .(Kinase, Kinase_entrez, Substrate)])
    tibble(
      motif_cut = motif_cut,
      func_cut  = func_cut,
      n_pairs   = nrow(pairs),
      n_kinases = uniqueN(pairs$Kinase_entrez),
      n_dark_pairs = sum(pairs$Kinase_entrez %in% dark_kin),
      pct_dark  = 100 * mean(pairs$Kinase_entrez %in% dark_kin)
    )
  })

write_csv(sweep, here("results", "threshold_sensitivity_sweep.csv"))

# Reconcile with the pipeline at the operating point: this sweep is an independent
# re-implementation, so agreement here is a check on both.
pipeline_numbers <- read_csv(here("results", "manuscript_numbers.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
pipeline_atlas_pairs <- as.integer(pipeline_numbers$value[pipeline_numbers$quantity == "pairs_atlas"])
sweep_at_operating_point <- sweep$n_pairs[sweep$motif_cut == motif_percentile_cutoff &
                                            sweep$func_cut == functional_score_cutoff]
message("Operating point: sweep = ", sweep_at_operating_point,
        " pairs; pipeline = ", pipeline_atlas_pairs, " pairs.")
knitr::kable(sweep, digits = 1)
```

## Evidence-layer orthogonality

*Addresses Reviewer 1, comment 4: are the information sources actually orthogonal,
and does HPA add anything beyond the Ochoa functional score?*


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ct <- read_csv(here("results", "filter_evidence_contingency.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
N <- sum(ct$n_site_kinase_pairs)

shannon <- function(p) { p <- p[p > 0]; -sum(p * log2(p)) }

layer_names <- c(coloc_ok = "HPA co-localization",
                 curated_site = "Curated site",
                 ochoa_high = "Functional score")

# marginal and joint distributions straight off the contingency table
marg_p <- function(v) as.numeric(tapply(ct$n_site_kinase_pairs, ct[[v]], sum)) / N
joint_p <- function(a, b) {
  as.numeric(tapply(ct$n_site_kinase_pairs, list(ct[[a]], ct[[b]]), sum)) %>%
    replace_na(0) %>% (function(x) x / N)
}

entropy_tbl <- tibble(
  layer = unname(layer_names[names(layer_names)]),
  entropy_bits = vapply(names(layer_names), function(v) shannon(marg_p(v)), numeric(1)),
  pass_rate = vapply(names(layer_names),
                     function(v) sum(ct$n_site_kinase_pairs[ct[[v]]]) / N, numeric(1))
)

mi_tbl <- combn(names(layer_names), 2, simplify = FALSE) %>%
  map_dfr(function(pr) {
    a <- pr[[1]]; b <- pr[[2]]
    mi <- shannon(marg_p(a)) + shannon(marg_p(b)) - shannon(joint_p(a, b))
    tibble(layer_a = unname(layer_names[a]),
           layer_b = unname(layer_names[b]),
           mi_bits = mi,
           normalised_redundancy = mi / min(shannon(marg_p(a)), shannon(marg_p(b))))
  })

write_csv(entropy_tbl, here("results", "evidence_layer_entropy.csv"))
write_csv(mi_tbl, here("results", "evidence_layer_mutual_information.csv"))
knitr::kable(entropy_tbl, digits = 4)
```

## Tissue-specificity coverage

*Addresses Reviewer 1, comment 3 (cell-type-specific proteins gain few predictions)
and Reviewer 2, comment 10 (most proteins are broadly expressed, so co-localization
filtering has limited discriminative power).*


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# HPA RNA tissue-specificity classification, extracted from the proteinatlas
# release (see data/hpa/README for provenance).
spec <- read_tsv(here("data", "hpa", "rna_tissue_specificity.tsv"),
                 show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  filter(rna_tissue_specificity != "", rna_tissue_specificity != "Not detected") %>%
  mutate(specificity = factor(
    rna_tissue_specificity,
    levels = c("Low tissue specificity", "Tissue enhanced",
               "Group enriched", "Tissue enriched")))

res <- read_csv(here("results", "combined_kinase_substrate_pairs_2025.csv"),
                show_col_types = FALSE)
curated_pairs <- res %>%
  filter(Source %in% c("PhosphoSitePlus", "EPSD", "iPTMNet")) %>%
  distinct(Kinase, Substrate)
atlas_pairs <- res %>% filter(Source == "Cantley") %>% distinct(Kinase, Substrate)
novel_pairs <- anti_join(atlas_pairs, curated_pairs, by = c("Kinase", "Substrate"))

substrate_status <- res %>%
  distinct(Substrate) %>%
  mutate(has_curated = Substrate %in% curated_pairs$Substrate,
         has_novel   = Substrate %in% novel_pairs$Substrate) %>%
  inner_join(spec %>% distinct(Gene, specificity), by = c("Substrate" = "Gene"))

tissue_tbl <- substrate_status %>%
  group_by(specificity) %>%
  summarise(n_substrates = n(),
            pct_with_novel = 100 * mean(has_novel),
            pct_curated_only = 100 * mean(has_curated & !has_novel),
            .groups = "drop")

# Background: how the whole proteome is distributed across these classes, which
# is the relevant denominator for Reviewer 2's point that most proteins are
# broadly expressed and so co-expression carries little discriminative power.
background_tbl <- spec %>%
  count(specificity, name = "n_genes") %>%
  mutate(pct_of_proteome = 100 * n_genes / sum(n_genes))

write_csv(tissue_tbl, here("results", "tissue_specificity_coverage.csv"))
write_csv(background_tbl, here("results", "tissue_specificity_background.csv"))
knitr::kable(background_tbl, digits = 1)
```
